remember: Measurement Book is K.P.W. Form 21; its register is K.P.W. Form 84 in the Divisional Office.
Only Executive/Assistant Engineers or executive subordinates in charge, issued books, may record detailed measurements.
Contractor signs after each set of measurements; an illiterate man gives thumb impression attested by an independent witness.

questions.q: Payments for works are based on measurements recorded in which form?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.9: measurements are recorded in Measurement Books, K.P.W. Form 21.

questions.q: In which form, and where, is the register of measurement books maintained?
options: K.P.W. Form 84, in the Divisional Office
K.P.W. Form 84, in the Sub-divisional Office
K.P.W. Form 21, in the Divisional Office
K.P.W. Form 90, in the Divisional Office
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.9: a register is maintained in K.P.W. Form 84 in the Divisional Office.

questions.q: Who may record detailed measurements?
options: Executive or Assistant Engineers, or executive subordinates in charge of works supplied with measurement books
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.11(a): only those officers to whom measurement books have been supplied may record them.

questions.q: How is the acceptance of an illiterate contractor taken in the measurement book?
options: Thumb impression attested by the Sub-divisional Officer
Thumb impression attested by an independent witness
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.11(d): thumb impression duly attested by an independent witness.

questions.q: How are the pages of each measurement book numbered?
options: Numbered by hand by the contractor
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.9: the pages of each book should be machine numbered.

remember: No blank pages left, no page torn out, no entry erased. Pages left blank by mistake are cancelled by diagonal lines and attested.
A cancelled measurement needs dated initials of the officer ordering it; each book has an up-to-date index.
Standard MBs: alphabetical series, kept by Divisional Accountant; certificates to Superintending Engineers on 30th April.

questions.q: How are pages left blank inadvertently in a measurement book dealt with?
options: Cancelled by diagonal lines, the cancellation being attested
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.11(e): blank pages must be cancelled by diagonal lines, attested.

questions.q: What supports the cancellation of a measurement entry?
options: Dated initials of the officer ordering the cancellation
Initials of the Divisional Accountant only
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.11(f): cancellation must be supported by dated initials of the officer ordering it.

questions.q: How are standard measurement books of a division numbered?
options: In a numerical series by year
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.13(2): numbered in an alphabetical series.

questions.q: Who keeps the original standard measurement books in personal custody?
options: The Executive Engineer, in his house
The Divisional Accountant, in the Division Office
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.13(2): personal custody of the Divisional Accountant in the Division Office.

questions.q: On what date each year do Divisional Officers send certificates to Superintending Engineers about standard measurement books?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.13(6): on 30th April each year.

remember: At least 25 per cent of measurement book entries are reviewed each year; 50 per cent of those selected get an arithmetic check by the Divisional Accountant.
Officers report page numbers of fresh entries to the Divisional Officer in the first week of the next month.
Reviewed pages are initialled, dated and marked 'Reviewed' by the Divisional Accountant.

questions.q: What minimum share of measurement book entries must be reviewed each year?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.14(b): at least twenty-five per cent of entries are reviewed each year.

questions.q: What share of the selected entries is also checked for arithmetical accuracy?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.14(b): arithmetical accuracy of 50 per cent of selected entries is checked.

questions.q: When do officers report page numbers of fresh entries to the Divisional Officer?
options: Within the first week of the succeeding month
Within the last week of the same month
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.14(c): within the first week of the succeeding month.

questions.q: What remark does the Divisional Accountant write on each page reviewed?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.14(h): every page reviewed is initialled and dated with remark 'Reviewed'.

remember: Muster roll is K.P.W. Form 19, for departmentally engaged day labourers; never prepared in duplicate; separate roll for each payment period.
Establishment-head employees are not paid on muster rolls.
Entries in indelible ink or copying pencil; attendance and fines in Part I; payment after passing by the Sub-divisional Officer.

questions.q: Muster rolls are prepared in which form?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6: muster rolls are prepared in K.P.W. Form 19.

questions.q: Whose pay is NOT drawn on muster rolls?
options: Employees of the division whose pay is charged to the head Establishment
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.4(1): permanent and temporary employees paid from the Establishment head are excluded.

questions.q: Can a muster roll be prepared in duplicate?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(a): muster rolls should never be prepared in duplicate.

questions.q: What may be used for entries in a muster roll?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(a) Note: indelible ink or copying pencil.

questions.q: Who passes a muster roll before payment is made?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(d): payment is made after the roll is passed by the Sub-divisional Officer.

remember: Unpaid wages are entered in register K.P.W. Form 19 A in the sub-division; later paid on Hand Receipt Form 24; unpaid three months are reported to the Divisional Officer.
Part II of muster roll records progress of measurable work.
Urgent casual labour on Hand Receipt: only by a Gazetted Officer or Upper Subordinate. Labour through contractor is objectionable; no MR or MB there.

questions.q: Which register records unpaid wage items?
options: Register of unpaid wages, K.P.W. Form 19 A
Register of measurement books, K.P.W. Form 84
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(d): unpaid items go in the register of unpaid wages K.P.W. Form 19 A.

questions.q: Later payments of unpaid wages are made on which form?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(e): subsequent payments on Hand Receipt K.P.W. Form 24.

questions.q: To whom are wages unpaid for three months reported?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(f): reported to the Divisional Officer.

questions.q: What is recorded in Part II of the muster roll?
options: Progress of work done by the labour, where it can be measured
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(g): Part II records progress of measurable work.

questions.q: Who may pay urgent casual labour on a Hand Receipt?
options: Only a Gazetted Officer or an Upper Subordinate
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.6(h): not except by a Gazetted Officer or an Upper Subordinate.

remember: Running contract: approximate quantity at a set price for a period; purchaser may take usually 25 per cent over or below.
Rate contract: stores at specified rates, usually no quantities; normally one year; notice to withdraw generally thirty days.
Running contracts settled by HODs and Departmental Purchase Committees; rate contracts only by Stores Purchase Department.

questions.q: What variation in quantity can the purchaser usually take in a running contract?
options: 25 per cent over or below the approximate quantity
questions.why: SPM 2013 13.2: usually 25 per cent over or below.

questions.q: Which contract usually mentions no quantities?
questions.why: SPM 2013 13.4: no quantities are usually mentioned in a rate contract.

questions.q: Who alone settles rate contracts?
questions.why: SPM 2013 13.6: rate contracts are settled by the Stores Purchase Department only.

questions.q: What is the normal period of a rate contract?
questions.why: SPM 2013 13.12: normally one year for stable technology products.

questions.q: What is the generally prescribed notice period to withdraw a rate contract?
questions.why: SPM 2013 13.15(iii): generally thirty days.

remember: Priced tender forms are essential for rate and running contracts irrespective of amount, unless Government decides otherwise.
It is obligatory for Departments to use Stores Purchase Department rate/running contracts.

questions.q: For rate and running contracts, are priced tender forms needed?
options: Yes, irrespective of the amount involved
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.30: priced tender forms are essential irrespective of amount unless Government decides otherwise.

questions.q: Is it obligatory for Departments to use Stores Purchase Department rate/running contracts?
questions.why: SPM 2013 13.9: obligatory for Government Departments.

questions.q: Who can alter the rule on priced tender forms for rate/running contracts?
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.30: 'unless otherwise decided by Government'.

remember: Tender if value is Rs. 1,00,000 or above; limited tender from Rs. 1 lakh to below Rs. 10 lakh with more than three firms; open tender as a general rule at Rs. 10 lakh or more.
Single tender only in unavoidable situations; telex/cable/fax quotations are rejected.
Tender form cost: cash, DD or M.O. only. Earnest money returned on opening day is receipted in Register of Tenders, Form 90.

questions.q: From what estimated value must tenders be invited?
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.7: tenders invited if value is Rs. 1,00,000 or above.

questions.q: How many supplier firms should a limited tender have?
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.10: more than three firms.

questions.q: Open tender is a general rule when the estimated value is at least:
What is done with quotations sent by telex, cable or facsimile?
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.23: such quotations are to be ignored and rejected.

questions.q: Which payment mode is NOT accepted for the cost of tender forms?
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.28: only cash, DD or M.O.; postal orders, stamps or bank cheques not accepted.

remember: A tender received late is excluded from consideration (SPM 2013 9.7).

questions.q: What happens to a tender that is received late?
options: It is accepted with a fine
It is accepted if the rate is lowest
questions.why: SPM 2013 9.7(f): tender received late is excluded.

questions.q: Which of these is a ground for excluding a tender?
options: It is sent by registered post on time
It is signed by the tenderer
questions.why: SPM 2013 9.7(f): late receipt of tender.

questions.q: A tender reaches the office after the closing time. What is the position?
options: It is considered with the others
It is returned for a fresh date
It is treated as a single tender
questions.why: SPM 2013 9.7(f): late tender is excluded.

remember: Bin Card balances are verified with the Priced Stores Ledger before physical verification; surplus treated as receipt, deficit as issue.
Deputy Chief Engineer (Stores and Purchase) does surprise verification yearly, at least 25% of costly items.
Deficit kept under Miscellaneous Public Works Advances; unserviceable stores need orders on Survey Report Form 17.

questions.q: What is done before an item is taken up for physical verification?
options: Item is issued to the site
Bin Card balance is verified with the Priced Stores Ledger
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.14: this verification is conducted before physical verification.

questions.q: Who does the surprise stores verification at least once a year?
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.35 Note (1): by the Deputy Chief Engineer (Stores and Purchase).

questions.q: What share of costly items such as cement, steel and bitumen is checked in surprise verification?
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.35 Note (1): at least 25% of stock of costly items.

questions.q: How is the value of a stock deficit kept?
options: Under Miscellaneous Public Works Advances pending recovery or adjustment
Written off by the Sub-divisional Officer
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.36(b): not charged off finally, kept under Misc. PW Advances.

questions.q: Which form is the Survey Report for removing unserviceable stores?
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.40: orders obtained on a Survey Report in K.P.W. Form 17.

remember: EMD is one percent of the cost of articles tendered, minimum Rs. 1,500; taken for tenders of Rs. 1,00,000 or more and special tenders.
EMD valid 45 days beyond final tender validity; forfeited on withdrawal or amendment within validity.
Returned to unsuccessful tenderers without interest within 30 days after conclusion of contract; exemption not for rate/running contracts.

questions.q: What is the EMD amount?
options: Five percent of the cost, minimum Rs. 1,500
One percent of the cost, minimum Rs. 15,000
Ten percent of the cost, minimum Rs. 1,000
One percent of the total cost of articles tendered, minimum Rs. 1,500
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.2: one percent, subject to minimum Rs. 1,500.

questions.q: Earnest money is ordinarily taken for every tender involving at least:
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.2: tenders of Rs. 1,00,000 or more and special tenders.

questions.q: For how long must EMD remain valid beyond the final tender validity period?
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.14: valid for 45 days beyond final tender validity.

questions.q: When is a tenderer's EMD forfeited?
options: If he quotes the lowest rate
If he asks for the tender form
If he withdraws or amends the tender within its validity period
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.15: forfeited on withdrawal or amendment within validity.

questions.q: Does the EMD exemption of registered firms apply to rate or running contract tenders?
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.6: exemption not applicable to Rate/Running Contract tenders.

remember: First and final bill: Form 22. Running account bill: Form 23. Running bill with secured advance: Form 23A. Hand Receipt: Form 24.
Final payments are made on forms printed on yellow paper, not used for intermediate payments.

questions.q: Which form is a first and final bill?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.16(a): First and final bill is K.P.W. Form 22.

questions.q: Which form is a running account bill?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.16(b): Running account bill is K.P.W. Form 23.

questions.q: Which form is a running account bill (Secured advance)?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.16(c): K.P.W. Form 23A.

questions.q: Which form is a Hand Receipt?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.16(d): Hand receipt is K.P.W. Form 24.

questions.q: On which colour of paper must forms for final payment be printed?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.20 Note: final payments on forms printed on yellow paper.

remember: Performance security: 5% of total contract value, for contract value above Rs. 1,00,000, from every successful bidder.
Furnished generally within 21 days after notification of award; valid 60 days beyond completion of all obligations.
EMD may be treated as part of it; only the balance is called for.

questions.q: What is the rate of performance security?
options: 5% of the total value of the contract
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.19: 5% of contract value rounded to nearest rupee.

questions.q: Performance security is taken for a contract value above:
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.17: contract value above Rs. 1,00,000.

questions.q: Within what time is performance security generally furnished after notification of award?
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.18: generally 21 days after notification of the award.

questions.q: How long does performance security remain valid beyond completion of contractual obligations?
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.18: valid 60 days beyond completion of all obligations.

questions.q: Can the EMD be treated as part of the performance security?
options: No, it must be refunded first
Yes, and the whole security is waived
Yes, and only the balance is called for
questions.why: SPM 2013 8.29: EMD may be treated as part of performance security; only balance called for.

remember: Sub-divisional Officers must checkmeasure all final bills on running accounts before payment.
Divisional Officers do at least 50 checkmeasurements in a financial year.
'Measured in my presence' is not a checkmeasurement. Object: detect errors and prevent fraudulent entries.

questions.q: Which bills must Sub-divisional Officers necessarily checkmeasure before payment?
options: All final bills on running accounts
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.15(1)(a): all final bills on running accounts.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of checkmeasurements by a Divisional Officer in a financial year?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.15(1)(c)(ii): at least 50 in a financial year.

questions.q: Is the entry 'measured in my presence' by a Sub-divisional Officer accepted as checkmeasurement?
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.15(1)(c)(vi): cannot be accepted as checkmeasurement.

questions.q: What is the object of checkmeasurement?
options: To detect errors in measurement and prevent fraudulent entries
questions.why: KPWAC 10.2.15(1)(c)(v): detect errors and prevent fraudulent entries.

remember: Stores up to Rs. 15,000 each occasion may be bought without quotation.
Rs. 15,000 to below Rs. 1,00,000: quotations, on recommendation of a three-member Local Purchase Committee.
Demand must not be split to avoid higher sanction.

questions.q: Up to what value can stores be bought on each occasion without inviting quotations?
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.3: up to Rs. 15,000 on each occasion.

questions.q: Who recommends purchases between Rs. 15,000 and Rs. 1 lakh?
options: A Local Purchase Committee of three members
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.4: Local Purchase Committee consisting of three members.

questions.q: Quotations may be invited if the estimated value of stores is:
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.6: between Rs. 15,000 to less than Rs. 1,00,000.

questions.q: Can demand for stores be divided into smaller quantities to avoid higher sanction?
options: Yes, for stores below Rs. 1 lakh
questions.why: SPM 2013 7.2: demand should not be divided for piece meal purchases to avoid sanction.

remember: Group I HODs may buy stores (not computers, peripherals, furniture) up to Rs. 20 lakh at a time; Group II and III up to Rs. 10 lakh.
Group I HODs usually purchase stores worth Rs. 1 crore or more a year.
Proposals above Rs. 6 crore up to Rs. 10 crore need approval of the Minister concerned after the Departmental Purchase Committee.

questions.q: How much can Group I HODs purchase at a time (other than computers and furniture)?
questions.why: SPM 2013 16.5: Group I up to Rs. 20 lakh at a time.

questions.q: What is the limit at a time for Group II and III Heads of Departments?
questions.why: SPM 2013 16.5: Rs. 10 lakh for Group II and III.

questions.q: Group I HODs usually purchase stores worth at least how much in a year?
questions.why: SPM 2013 16.1: Rs. 1 crore or more in a year.

questions.q: Who approves proposals above Rs. 6 crore up to Rs. 10 crore after the Departmental Purchase Committee?
questions.why: SPM 2013 16.9: approval of the Minister concerned.

remember: Lump sum contract bills use K.P.W. Forms 23 B and 22A.
Government sanction is needed in each case for a work on lump sum basis.

questions.q: Which forms are used for bills of lump sum contracts?
questions.why: KPWAC 11.5.1: Forms 23 B and 22A.

questions.q: Whose sanction is needed to execute a work on lump sum basis?
questions.why: KPWAC 11.2.3: sanction from Government in each case.

questions.q: Can a work be executed on lump sum basis without Government sanction?
questions.why: KPWAC 11.2.3: no work through lump sum basis unless Government sanctions it in each case.

remember: Before ordering, first use surplus stock with other Government Departments, irrespective of its cost.
The purchasing officer must satisfy himself that funds are available and valid administrative sanction exists.

questions.q: What must be done before ordering new stores?
options: Use surplus stock available with other Departments first
questions.why: SPM 2013 6.3: surplus stock of other Departments should first be utilized.

questions.q: Does the cost at which surplus stock is available matter?
options: No, it is utilized irrespective of cost
Yes, only if approved by Finance
questions.why: SPM 2013 6.3: utilized irrespective of the cost.

questions.q: What must a purchasing officer satisfy himself about before buying?
options: The supplier is a registered firm
Funds are available and valid administrative sanction exists
questions.why: SPM 2013 6.5: funds available and valid administrative sanction.

remember: A Purchasing Officer can buy articles worth Rs. 50,000 through GeM without quotation or tenders.
Demand for goods must not be divided into small quantities.

questions.q: Up to what value can a Purchasing Officer buy through GeM without quotation or tender?
questions.why: SPM Amendment 2018, 19.5: articles worth Rs. 50,000 through GeM.

questions.q: Can demand for goods be divided into small quantities to avoid GeM bidding?
questions.why: SPM Amendment 2018, 19.9: demand shall not be divided into small quantities.

questions.q: Which portal allows purchase of Rs. 50,000 articles without quotation or tenders?
questions.why: SPM Amendment 2018, 19.5: purchase through GeM.

remember: Bin Card, K.P.W. Form No.7, keeps a chronological record of receipts, issues and running balance of each article of stock.

questions.q: Which card records receipts, issues and running balance of each stock article?
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.12: kept in the Bin Card K.P.W. Form No.7.

questions.q: What is the form number of the Bin Card?
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.12: Bin Card K.P.W. Form No.7.

questions.q: How is the record in a Bin Card kept?
questions.why: KPWAC 7.2.12: a chronological record of receipts, issues and running balance.
